title: XI. Canons concerning good angels and their governance
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): smoke, plus stench — ye heat belonging toward anger plus envy, ye smoke belonging toward pride, ye stench belonging toward luxury — yet among vices they most hate heat. Fifth, angels turn away out from whatever smells belonging toward vice; Fourth, angels stand as not to be adored (Revelation 19:10). Zanchi). Acts 12:15; Matthew 18:10; Third, a human being has not only one guardian angel but many at once (Psalm 91:11; Second, angels serve each person plus each order (Psalm 34:8). First, ye confirmation belonging toward angels in ye good was not a wages owed to some merit, but ye free reward belonging toward most liberal God (Romans 11:35). Canons stand as to be observed concerning good angels plus their governance. XI.
pass_b_english: XI. Canons are to be observed concerning good angels and their governance. First, the confirmation of angels in the good was not a wages owed to some merit, but the free reward of most liberal God (Romans 11:35). Second, angels serve each person and each order (Psalm 34:8). Third, a human being has not only one guardian angel but many at once (Psalm 91:11; Matthew 18:10; Acts 12:15; Zanchi). Fourth, angels are not to be adored (Revelation 19:10). Fifth, angels turn away from whatever smells of vice; yet among vices they most hate heat, smoke, and stench — the heat of anger and envy, the smoke of pride, the stench of luxury.
source_text: XI. Sunt autem de bonis angelis eorumque gubernatione observandi canones. 1. Angelorum in bono confirmatio non fuit debitum meriti alicuius stipendium, sed gratuitum Dei liberalissimi praemium (Rom. 11:35). 2. Angeli cuique et homini et ordini inserviunt (Psal. 34:8). 3. Homo non unum duntaxat Angelum custodem, sed multos simul habet (Psal. 91:11; Matth. 18:10; Act. 12:15; Zanchius). 4. Angeli non sunt adorandi (Apoc. 19:10). 5. Aversantur Angeli quicquid vitium redolet; maxime tamen oderunt in vitiis calorem, fumum, foetorem — calorem irae et invidiae, fumum superbiae, foetorem luxuriae.
